geometry_edits.rationale: Broaden the access-side notch so the blue-edge threshold becomes a clearer public void rather than a thin incision.
Increase the notch depth to make the ground-level opening more legible in plan and elevation.
Extend the threshold cut upward slightly so the entry seam reads across more of the building height.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent compact mass with a dominant bar-like body and a legible notch/slot along the access edge, so it avoids the worst fragmentation and supports the neighborhood-living brief. Parcel response is acceptable: the form sits inside the boundary and does not merely fill the box, and the main gesture is diagonally oriented rather than arbitrary. The thick blue access edge is answered only weakly, though: the west-side notch is present but small relative to the mass, so the public threshold is legible but underdeveloped. In all four views the object is internally consistent and the silhouettes agree reasonably well; there is no obvious cross-view collision. The main weakness is that the void is too slight to become a convincing public court/entry sequence, and the roof/section remains fairly generic for a program that benefits from a more expressive ground threshold or terrace logic. The form is program-plausible for neighborhood mixed-use, but only moderately so; it feels closer to a compact block with a trim cut than to an active, socially porous street building.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion-like and culturally expressive than this neighborhood-living brief; avoid over-specializing to gallery-like transparency.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a central void and a bridge-like connector can create a legible public threshold while keeping the overall object compact.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger campus scale and tower context; do not imitate the density or multi-building complexity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/courtyard campus composition shows how multiple masses can organize a shared open center without losing hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is more compact and less openly glazed; keep the massing logic, not the material expression.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A horizontal bar with a carved central void and slight roof articulation can support neighborhood retail/mixed-use logic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more landscape-driven and spread out; candidate should remain a single compact mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, bridge-connected composition with a central court suggests a good model for active circulation and shared open space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference reads more like a campus; candidate should be simpler and more continuous.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking blocks with a courtyard and upper bridging can preserve ground-level public life while differentiating upper mass.

warnings: Visible access response is present but shallow; it needs a stronger public void or entry seam at the blue frontage.
The section is mostly generic and could support the program better with a more articulated carve, terrace, or lift.
Do not over-iterate into fragmentation; preserve the dominant compact mass.
